text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela was born in Mvezo, in the Eastern Cape, on 18 July 1918. [D]

Mandela was convicted with seven co-accused in the Rivonia Trial on 11 June 1964 and sentenced to life imprisonment the next day. He was held on Robben Island, moved to Pollsmoor Prison on 31 March 1982 and to Victor Verster Prison near Paarl on 7 December 1988, and was released from Victor Verster on 11 February 1990. [D]
In 1985 Mandela had prostate surgery while imprisoned. His urologist said in July 2001 that the gland had been enlarged and was causing a urinary blockage, and that part of it was removed. [D]

Mandela was taken to hospital on 12 August 1988 and diagnosed with tuberculosis; public reports describe it as early tuberculosis, treated at the Constantiaberg Medi-clinic, after which he was moved to Victor Verster Prison. [D]

His doctors said publicly in 2001 that he had been monitored regularly with the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test, that a slight rise in the PSA led to a biopsy of the prostate, and that the biopsy confirmed microscopic cancer within the gland. News reports said the raised blood level was first found in November 2000. [D]
Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's first democratically elected president on 10 May 1994 and stepped down in 1999 after one term. [D]
